statements.t: As we continue to define the resource base, we have essentially already positioned ourselves as a future upstream provider, with roughly three quarters of anticipated oxide revenue tied to demand in the semiconductor industry.
As we move toward that goal, we are well financed to advance the project through all stages of development up to the commencement of construction of the refinery.
We expect the pre-feasibility study to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and be completed later next year.
As bench-scale metallurgical results become available, including from new e-waste samples, we also anticipate completion of the pilot plant in the second half of 2027.

On the downstream critical mineral front, we also remain in advanced discussions regarding potential domestic and international critical mineral offtake transactions, as well as project financing for the refinery involving the public and private sectors.
We anticipate stronger margin expansion in both the fourth quarter of 2026 and full-year 2027.

We are continuing our coal production growth, and expect the third section at Berwind and the first underground section at Maben to be in production before year-end, adding roughly 0.6 million tons of annualized low-vol production.
Including the restart of our Laurel Fork Mine, we will have added almost 1 million annualized low-vol tons this year.
We are well positioned for 2027 on forward sales, having committed a strong portion of our anticipated production.

We currently have no borrowings under our revolving credit facility and expect a working capital tailwind to increase further liquidity over the coming quarters as we sell inventory stockpiled for sale into higher-priced markets and convert those tons to cash.”

The remaining increase is attributable to the development of our rare earth element and critical minerals project.

In addition to this matter, the increase in 2026 was also due to an increase in labor costs of $7.3 million, including stock compensation, with the remaining increase attributable to costs associated with our internal reorganization and the development of our rare earth element and critical minerals project.
We expect metallurgical coal prices to remain volatile in the near term.
The Company currently expects to continue declaring dividends on its Class B common stock in the future.

Our primary use of cash includes capital expenditures for mine development, infrastructure and equipment, ongoing operating expenses, as well as our investment in advancing our rare earth elements and other critical minerals project.

As of the date of this Quarterly Report, we expect to fund our capital and liquidity requirements for the next twelve months and the reasonably foreseeable future with cash on hand, borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility, and projected cash flows from operations.
